approachQuestion.prompt:
Packet Order
An array has n records with distinct sequence numbers. Every record is at most d positions from its position in sorted order. Return records in increasing sequence order. Example: [3,1,2,5,4], d=2 → [1,2,3,4,5].

2 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ d < n. Comparisons and record copies take constant time. Input is read-only and random-access. Output is separate. The displacement promise is guaranteed. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ d < n. Comparisons and record copies take constant time. Input is read-only and random-access. Output is separate. The displacement promise is guaranteed.

options.text: Build a min-heap of the first d+1 records. Emit its minimum, insert the next unread record if any remains, and repeat until both the unread suffix and heap are empty.
options.feedback: The next sorted record cannot lie more than d positions ahead of its final position, so it is among these buffered candidates.

options.text: Copy all records and comparison-sort the copy.
options.feedback: This is correct but ignores the displacement promise and retains more candidates when d is small.

options.text: Use the same procedure with only d initial records.
options.feedback: For [2,3,1], d=2, the initial buffer omits 1 and wrongly emits 2 first.

options.text: Swap each adjacent inversion once in one left-to-right pass.
options.feedback: For [3,2,1], d=2, one pass leaves [2,1,3], still unordered.

Displacement at most d means the next output lies among d+1 unseen candidates. After emitting one, add one new record. A full-input heap is correct but ignores the bounded-frontier storage benefit.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A with bottom-up binary-heap construction and iterative repairs. Let n and d be as above; at most d+1 records are buffered. Each emitted record is copied once to separate output. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n log(d+2)) time, O(d+1) auxiliary space
O(n log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Maintain only d+1 candidate records while emitting n outputs.
details: The initial copy/build is O(d+1); n emissions can each need a heap-height repair. Displaced blocks can force such repairs throughout, giving O(n log(d+2)) worst-case time. The heap uses O(d+1) working records. Output writes are linear and output storage is excluded.
“O(n) time, O(d+1) auxiliary space”: The frontier still requires repairs and d is variable.
“O(n log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This loose sorting bound loses the dependence on displacement.
“O(nd) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method stores a heap rather than scanning a window for each output.
